title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is p.3 of a typed letter from 1965, written to a 'tu' correspondent (very probably Serre). It is an early, pre-Bombay version of what became the standard conjectures.

Notation, from the surrounding pages:
- X is smooth projective of dimension n over an algebraically closed field; Y is a smooth hyperplane section; ξ is the hyperplane class.
- C^i(X) is the Q-vector space of codimension-i cycles modulo 'τ-equivalence'. The prose ('cycle à coeff. rationnels', 'τ-équivalence = équivalence numérique (= homologique, coincée entre les deux)', and next page 'cohomologiquement équivalent à 0 ⇒ τ-équivalent à 0') shows τ is finer than homological equivalence. It is evidently algebraic equivalence modulo torsion, in the spirit of Pic^τ.
- Conjecture A is a Lefschetz-type statement for cycles: ξ^{n-2i}: C^i → C^{n-i} is bijective, or at least the relevant maps are bijective/surjective.
- A' is a 'weak Lefschetz' for cycles: C^i(Y) → C^{i+1}(X) is surjective for 2i ≥ n-1.
- B is the Hodge-index-type positivity of (-1)^m ε(xx') on the primitive part P^m(X) = ker(ξ: C^m → C^{m+1}) when n = 2m.

Consequences of A + B listed on this page:
1. The C^i(X) are finite-dimensional; the τ-groups are even of finite type.
2. Hence C^m(X)⊗_Q Q_ℓ → H^{2m}(X)(m) is injective, so rank C^m ≤ b_{2m}. Positivity forces τ = numerical = homological.
3. The category of motives generated by smooth projective varieties is semisimple. Concretely, the Q-algebra of correspondences on X modulo τ is finite semisimple, with a positive involution and trace.
4. A 'generalized A': for an algebraic correspondence f inducing H^{2i}(X) → H^{2i+2r}(X') and C^i(X) → C^{i+r}(X'), a cycle on X' lies in f(C^i(X)) iff its class lies in f(H^{2i}(X)).
   - Proof sketch using semisimplicity: there is an algebraic g with fgf = f. If cl(x) = f(h), then cl(fg x) = fgf h = f h = cl(x), so x = f(gx) because τ = homological.
5. Semisimplicity of motives implies semisimplicity of the Galois action in the Tate conjecture.
6. A + B should give a theory of the abelian varieties parametrizing continuous families of cycles. These are 'intermediate Jacobians', the algebraic pieces of Weil's intermediate Jacobians, related to odd-degree cohomology. He suspects that proving B may already require these abelian varieties.

Strategy and A''. He proposes to attack A and A' first. He gives the equivalent form A'': for the affine open U = X − Y, C^i(U) = 0 whenever 2i > n.
- The equivalence with A' is the localization exact sequence C^{i-1}(Y) → C^i(X) → C^i(U) → 0, with the index shift 2(i-1) ≥ n-1 ⇔ 2i > n. This is correct.
- On cohomology, A'' is the cycle analogue of Artin vanishing: H^{2i}(U) = 0 for 2i > n.
- The next page generalizes to: on any smooth variety, cohomologically trivial ⇒ τ-trivial. It then asks for a method to 'push cycles to infinity'.
errors: With hindsight, the τ-equivalence (algebraic equivalence ⊗Q) versions are false. Griffiths (1969) showed algebraic ≠ homological equivalence for 1-cycles on the generic quintic threefold. This kills 'τ = numérique' and the next page's 'cohomologically trivial ⇒ τ-trivial'.

Clemens (1983): the Griffiths group ⊗Q of the generic quintic threefold has infinite rank. This refutes 'les groupes de classes de cycles pour la τ-équivalence sont de type fini'. It also refutes A', A'' (n=3, i=2) and hence A in the τ-version. The image of NS(Y) for a fixed hyperplane section Y has finite rank, so it cannot account for the whole Griffiths group.

The statements remain sensible if τ is replaced by homological equivalence, which is what Grothendieck did in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968). The previous page already notes this option ('se borner à énoncer A pour l'équivalence cohomologique'), at the cost of A's 'purely geometric' character.
Minor: 'Notes aussi' should be 'Note(z) aussi'; this is a typo in the original.

ideas.what: Positivity plus Lefschetz conjectures imply finite-dimensionality of cycle groups, numerical = homological equivalence, and injectivity of the cycle map from cycles ⊗ Q_ℓ, with rank C^m ≤ b_{2m}
ideas.modern_name: Consequences of the standard conjectures B and Hodge type (implying conjecture D)

ideas.what: Semisimplicity of the category of motives and of the correspondence algebra, with positive involution and trace
ideas.where_published: Discussed in Kleiman's and Manin's expositions of Grothendieck's motives; Bombay text

ideas.what: Semisimplicity of motives implies semisimplicity of the Galois action in the Tate conjecture
ideas.modern_name: Galois semisimplicity part of Tate's conjecture

ideas.what: A cycle lies in the image of an algebraic correspondence iff its cohomology class lies in the cohomological image, deduced from semisimplicity via a quasi-inverse g with fgf = f
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic splitting of correspondences under the standard conjectures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore consequence of the standard conjectures

ideas.what: Abelian varieties parametrizing algebraically trivial cycles as the algebraic parts of Weil intermediate Jacobians, tied to odd cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic representatives / Lieberman's algebraic part of intermediate Jacobian; Murre's theorem
ideas.where_published: Theme alluded to in Grothendieck's 'Hodge's general conjecture is false for trivial reasons' (1969)

ideas.what: Reduction of hard Lefschetz for cycles (A) to a weak-Lefschetz surjectivity C^i(Y) → C^{i+1}(X) (A'), restated as vanishing of cycle groups above middle codimension on the affine complement U = X − Y (A'')
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture via weak Lefschetz / Artin-vanishing analogue for Chow groups of affine varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standardly attributed; related ideas in Beilinson's 'Remarks on Grothendieck's standard conjectures' (2012) and work on Chow groups of affine varieties (Murthy, Srinivas)

missed.claim: Documentary evidence that in 1965 Grothendieck formulated the Lefschetz/Hodge-type conjectures for algebraic equivalence ⊗Q ('τ-équivalence'). He explicitly expected τ = numerical equivalence and finite generation of cycle groups. Griffiths (1969) and Clemens (1983) refute this, and the shift to homological equivalence in the Bombay text is a retreat. The letter dates and documents the original, stronger, false form.
missed.quote: τ-équivalence = équivalence numérique ... les groupes de classes de cycles pour la τ-équivalence sont de type fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Clarifies the genesis of the standard conjectures and why the published version uses homological equivalence; useful for the history of motives.

missed.claim: Conjecture A'' as a route to the Lefschetz standard conjecture: cycles of codimension > n/2 on the affine complement of a hyperplane section vanish (homological version), via 'pushing cycles to infinity'. The weak-Lefschetz/affine-vanishing reformulation of the Lefschetz conjecture is not a standard approach in the literature.
missed.quote: Soit U l'ouvert affine (de dimension n) X-Y, alors C^i(U)=0 pour tout i tel que 2i > n.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A homological-equivalence variant (algebraic classes on X in degree > n restricted to U) offers a geometric, moving-lemma-style angle on the Lefschetz standard conjecture. It is related to, but not identical with, Beilinson's 2012 reductions.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly the known consequences of the standard conjectures, in an early letter. The historically notable points are the original τ- (algebraic-equivalence) formulation, which Griffiths and Clemens later refuted, and the affine-vanishing reformulation A'' of the Lefschetz conjecture, which I do not recall seeing in print in this form.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten correction near 'C^m(X)⊗_Q Q_ℓ' is rendered correctly as tensor over Q with Q_ℓ.
'Notes aussi' is faithful to the typescript (original typo).
